s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory and skin symptoms with a progressive rash
salient_findings: Pseudovesicular papules with superficial crusting on the trunk
key_facts: Age of the patient is in the 60s
Initial symptoms include asthenia, anorexia, and cough
Hospitalization occurred six days after symptom onset
Papules were asymptomatic and appeared on the trunk
Papules evolved to a purpuric rash within 48 hours
Nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 was negative
Immunohistochemical testing for herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses was negative
Histologic analysis showed extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis
Large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration were present
Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis and large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive rash with purpuric evolution and mucocutaneous involvement suggested by systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic papules evolving to purpuric rash and histologic findings of epidermal necrosis

shortlist.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric rash and dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of skin symptoms with papulovesicular eruption and systemic involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including the initial papulovesicular eruption that evolved into a purpuric rash, along with the histologic findings of extensive epidermal necrosis, acantholysis, and large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration, are consistent with Stevens-Johnson syndrome, a severe skin and mucous membrane disorder often triggered by infections or medications.

rejected.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
rejected.why: While similar to Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis typically involves more widespread skin detachment and is often associated with medication use, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is more common in children and is characterized by a distinctive scalded appearance of the skin, which is not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by palpable purpura, abdominal pain, and arthritis, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: While erythema multiforme can present with skin lesions, the presence of extensive epidermal necrosis and the evolution of the rash are more consistent with Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
